faqs.question: What's the difference between a corporate website and a regular business website?
faqs.answer: A corporate website is built for an established, often larger organization with multiple departments, leadership, and external stakeholders to represent. It carries deeper sections — leadership, governance, careers, news, investor or partner pages — and a content structure several teams can manage. A standard business website is usually leaner and focused mainly on generating enquiries.

faqs.question: Can our marketing and HR teams update content without a developer?
faqs.answer: Yes. We build on a content management system with clear templates, so your teams can publish press releases, update leadership bios, and post job openings themselves. We hand over the admin access and train your staff, so routine updates never wait on us.

faqs.question: Do we fully own the corporate website after it launches?
faqs.answer: Completely. You receive the source code, design files, the CMS, hosting and domain accounts, and documentation at handover, with no lock-in. The site is yours to keep, move to another provider, or extend in-house whenever you choose.

faqs.question: Can you build the site in both Arabic and English with RTL?
faqs.answer: Yes. We deliver native Arabic and English experiences with full right-to-left support, not machine translation. Both language versions share one structure, so your team manages and publishes content once across both audiences.

faqs.question: How does the project start, and is there any commitment upfront?
faqs.answer: We begin with a free consultation to map your departments, stakeholders, and content needs, then prepare a written scope. You also see a demo preview of the design before you commit, so there are no surprises and no obligation to proceed until you're confident.
